title: Exact Flags
statement: A monitoring system records integer readings. A reading is flagged when it is odd; negative odd numbers such as -3 are flagged too. A stretch is a non-empty run of consecutive readings, and two stretches are different when their positions differ, even if their values match. Return how many stretches contain exactly k flagged readings.

examples.explanation: Flagged readings are at positions 0, 2 and 4. The stretches with exactly two are positions 0-2, 0-3, 1-4 and 2-4.
No reading is flagged, so every one of the 6 stretches has zero flagged readings.

hints.content: Replace each reading by 1 if it is flagged and 0 otherwise. Only the number of ones in a stretch matters.
Counting windows with exactly k ones directly is awkward: shrinking or growing a window can jump over valid sizes, and a two-pointer window is not monotone in the exact count.
Counting windows with at most k ones is easy. For each right end, the valid left ends form one contiguous range, and that range only moves right as the right end advances.
exactly(k) = atMost(k) - atMost(k - 1). When k is 0, atMost(-1) is 0.
For atMost(limit): add the right reading, move left forward while the flagged count exceeds limit, then add right - left + 1 stretches ending at right. Each reading enters and leaves the window once.

testCases.explanation: Four stretches contain two flagged readings.
All six stretches have no flagged readings.
k = 0 with the only stretch flagged.
k larger than the number of flagged readings gives 0.
Gaps of unflagged readings multiply the number of valid stretches.
Values at the extremes of the range.
A large random mix with about half the readings flagged.
A large mostly unflagged input counted with k = 0.

solutions.title: Count every stretch
solutions.intuition: Fix a start, extend the end one reading at a time with a running flagged count, and count the stretches that hit k.
solutions.approach: Two nested loops over start and end. Track the flagged count while extending, and increment the answer whenever it equals k.
solutions.pseudocode:
total = 0
for start: flagged = 0
  for end >= start: flagged += isOdd(readings[end]); if flagged == k: total += 1
commonMistakes: Resetting the running count at the wrong level.
Using x % 2 === 1, which misses negative odd numbers because -3 % 2 is -1.
solutions.interviewExplanation: Every stretch is identified by its start and end, and a running flagged count makes each extension O(1), so there are n(n+1)/2 steps. It is correct for any k but quadratic for 10,000 readings.

steps.title: Start at position 0
steps.content: In [1, 2, 3, 4, 5] with k = 2, ends 2 and 3 reach exactly two flagged readings.

solutions.title: Count earlier prefixes with the right flagged total
solutions.intuition: A stretch has exactly k flagged readings when two prefix flagged totals differ by k.
solutions.approach: Keep seen[c], the number of prefixes with flagged total c. At each position, the stretches ending here with exactly k flagged readings start right after a prefix with total (current - k), so add seen[current - k], then record the current total.
solutions.pseudocode:
seen = [0]*(n+1); seen[0] = 1; flagged = 0; total = 0
for x in readings: flagged += isOdd(x)
  if flagged >= k: total += seen[flagged - k]
  seen[flagged] += 1
commonMistakes: Forgetting to count the empty prefix (seen[0] = 1).
Updating seen before reading it when k = 0.
solutions.interviewExplanation: This is the prefix-sum counting idea specialised to a bounded counter, so a plain array replaces the hash map. It is linear in time but uses O(n) memory, while the two-window approach uses O(1) extra memory.

steps.title: Prefix totals
steps.content: For [1, 2, 3, 4, 5] the flagged totals after each reading are 1, 1, 2, 2, 3 (plus 0 for the empty prefix).

steps.title: Match differences
steps.content: With k = 2, each end pairs with earlier prefixes whose total is 2 less, giving 4 stretches.

solutions.title: atMost(k) minus atMost(k - 1) with a sliding window
solutions.intuition: At most k flagged readings is monotone in the window, so a variable window counts it in one pass; the exact count is the difference of two such counts.
solutions.approach: Write atMost(limit) with a left pointer: for each right end, add the reading, move left while the flagged count exceeds limit, and add right - left + 1. Return atMost(k) - atMost(k - 1), treating a negative limit as 0.
solutions.pseudocode:
atMost(limit): if limit < 0: return 0
  left = 0; flagged = 0; count = 0
  for right: flagged += isOdd(r[right]); while flagged > limit: flagged -= isOdd(r[left]); left += 1
             count += right - left + 1
return atMost(k) - atMost(k - 1)
commonMistakes: Calling atMost(k - 1) with k = 0 and entering the loop with a negative limit.
Counting only the longest window per right end instead of all valid left ends.
Testing odd with value % 2 === 1, which fails for negative numbers.
solutions.interviewExplanation: For a fixed right end, every start from left to right gives a stretch with at most limit flagged readings, because removing readings from the left never raises the count. That makes a two-pointer window valid, and each pointer moves only forward, so atMost runs in O(n). Stretches with exactly k are the ones with at most k minus the ones with at most k - 1. Two passes, constant extra memory.

steps.title: atMost(2) on [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
steps.content: Valid stretches ending at each position are 1, 2, 3, 4, 4, so atMost(2) = 14.

steps.title: atMost(1)
steps.content: The same pass with limit 1 counts 1, 2, 2, 3, 2, so atMost(1) = 10 and the answer is 14 - 10 = 4.
